title: No Exact Path for Electrons? Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
To check a tyre's pressure you must let a little air out, and a big thermometer cools a tiny drop of hot water. Measuring something can change it. For an electron, that problem is the whole story. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 2, Structure of Atom) we follow Aarav from the cycle shop to Heisenberg's uncertainty principle.

On the molecule bench, we try to see one electron with light. A long wavelength photon is gentle but gives a blurry position; a short wavelength photon pins the electron down but kicks it hard. A live chart shows that squeezing the position uncertainty stretches the momentum uncertainty, and their product never drops below h/4pi. We build the principle step by step (delta x times delta p >= h/4pi, delta x times delta v >= h/4pi m), compare a 1 mg grain (about 10^-28) with an electron (about 10^-4 m^2 s^-1), and work out the velocity uncertainty of an electron located within one atom (at least 5.79 x 10^5 m/s). Then why fixed Bohr orbits had to go, the exam trap about instruments, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 20 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
